problem.text: Sidorenko-type inequalities for directed graphs on two-sided correlation kernels of finite groups, equivalently for directed 1-subdivisions on product Cayley kernels.

claims.text: Theorem 1.1: for every finite group, every real function f and every finite directed graph F, t(F, C_f) >= (E f)^{2 e(F)}, where C_f(x,y) = E_z f(x^{-1} z) f(z y^{-1}). Corollary 4.1: the directed 1-subdivision of every directed graph satisfies the inequality on the product kernel f(xy). Remark 4.2: this contains the 1-subdivision theorem for conjugacy-averaged Cayley kernels.

assumptions.text: Finite groups with uniform measure; real-valued functions.

methods.text: Fourier expansion over irreducible representations; the average over each subdivision vertex forces contragredient pairs and gives a positive semidefinite edge block; vertex averages are commuting orthogonal projections.

limitations.text: Only kernels of the correlation or product form on finite groups.

relevance.text: No result of this paper decides the statement or a declared neighbour. For the 1-subdivision neighbours it gives a further restricted host class (product Cayley kernels) on which every 1-subdivision satisfies the inequality.
